MyVNC: how this repository works

repo-blueprint 0.14.0. Generated from tooling/gates.yaml, .agents/ and AGENTS.md by tooling/scripts/render-overview.mjs.

From idea to release

Work starts as a ticket or a proposal, becomes a phase with a plan, and is delivered one chunk at a time: one agent session, one commit. Hooks run checks on every edit and at the end of every turn; git hooks run them on commit and push; the full CI runs locally in a container and on self-hosted runners. Choices only the owner can make go to project/review-queue.md, work that needs owner authority to project/handoffs/.

Agents

Instructions live in AGENTS.md (Claude Code reads it through CLAUDE.md). Roles and skills live in .agents/; Codex reads the skills there directly, Claude Code gets generated copies in .claude/.

TierClaude Code modelCodex model and effort
T1 fasthaikuinherit, effort low
T2 standardsonnetinherit, effort medium
T3 deepopusinherit, effort high

Roles

RoleTierUse
architectT3Designs and challenges cross-cutting changes - ADRs, contracts, data models, security boundaries - and writes the plan with verifiable chunks. Use before implementation when a change is architecture-significant.
doc-writerT2Writes and updates documentation in docs/ and project/ with valid front-matter. Use for reader docs, status updates, release notes and test protocols.
implementerT2Implements one chunk of a planned phase (at most 5 files) including its tests. Use for well-specified code changes inside one package or app.
reviewerT3Independent read-only review of a diff for correctness, security and contract drift. Use before merge for anything that touches a trust boundary, a public contract or more than one package.
scoutT1Read-only search across the repository. Use to locate files, symbols, callers and conventions before changing code, so the main agent keeps a clean context. Returns paths with line numbers and a short conclusion, never file dumps.
test-runnerT1Runs substantial gates and test suites and returns failures, with file:line and a one-line likely cause. Delegate long or noisy runs; keep short checks in the main agent.

Skills

SkillUse
chunk-workflowThe loop for implementing one chunk of a phase from start to commit. Use whenever you start work on a chunk, or when a task is about to grow beyond one chunk.
cve-triageTriage of vulnerability findings from Zot image scans or dependency audits. Use when a gate or the weekly surveillance reports a CVE.
debug-loopBounded debugging procedure. Use when a bug, failing test or broken gate is not fixed by the first obvious change.
new-phasePlans a new delivery phase from a ticket or a proposal in project/proposals/. Use when the owner promotes work into a phase or asks for a phase plan.
releasePrepares and verifies a release - version, changelog, release note, test protocol, image scan in Zot and DocSaga sync. Use only when the owner asks for a release; tagging and pushing are hard stops.
setup-machineInstalls the tools, dependencies and git hooks this repository's local gates need on the owner's machine. Use only when the owner asks to install dependencies or set up the machine, or answers yes to the doctor's suggestion.
update-blueprintUpdates this repository to a newer repo-blueprint version - dry run, apply, hand-merge of locally changed files, migration steps, regeneration and verification. Use when the session start or blueprint-status reports a newer blueprint and the owner asks for the update.

HookWhenWhat
session-start.mjsSession startBranch, uncommitted changes, open owner decisions, STATUS.md and a newer blueprint into the context; stages last session's metrics

Where things go

FolderPurpose

docs/assets/Images for the docs
docs/explanation/How and why the product works
project/handoffs/Work waiting for owner authority
project/proposals/Ideas and designs before a phase

project/reviews/Dated assessments: security, CVE, architecture

Names follow the naming standard: English kebab-case, dates first, the folder carries the type (gate names).

Hard stops

  • git push, force push, rebase of shared branches, tags, --no-verify
  • Version bumps and releases; deploys
  • New or upgraded dependencies, CI, hooks, registries, base images (installing from the existing lockfiles
  • Breaking API or contract changes, auth/permission/crypto changes, migrations
  • Deleting files or data you did not create; network calls to non-local services
  • Changing an accepted ADR (write a superseding ADR instead)
  • Secrets: never print, commit or write them; use Infisical where configured

CI

Full CI on the developer machine: node tooling/scripts/ci-local.mjs (the ci stage in a container with every scanner). Workflows: .github/workflows/ci.yml.
